chunks.title: LEQ exemplar — LEQ3/Set2 Sample 3A, score 6/6
chunks.content: LEQ (how sectional tensions shaped US society, 1800–1848) scored 6/6. Thesis (1): sectional tensions led to political debates over slavery's expansion into western territories. Contextualization (1): Middle Passage, southern slavery, the North's gradual abandonment. Evidence (2): annexation of Texas, Free Soil Party, Missouri Compromise — used to support the argument. Analysis & Reasoning (2): comparison (Free Soil vs. popular sovereignty) and causation (Missouri Compromise → tension) AND complex understanding via four pieces of evidence (King Cotton, Texas, Missouri Compromise, Free Soil) supporting a nuanced argument.

chunks.title: LEQ exemplar — LEQ3/Set2 Sample 3B, score 4/6
chunks.content: LEQ scored 4/6 (Thesis 1, Contextualization 1, Evidence 1, Analysis & Reasoning 1). Thesis (1): regional differences in slavery and economics created society-changing tensions. Contextualization (1): post-period examples (Bleeding Kansas, Lincoln's election, Reconstruction Amendments). Evidence (1): southern slavery vs. northern manufacturing/railroads described but not used to support an argument, so caps at 1. Analysis & Reasoning (1): comparison of North/South economies, but the multiple-perspectives attempt lacks nuance so no complex understanding.
